Patients must have histologically confirmed glioblastoma (IDH wild-type, MGMT promoter methylated) that has undergone resection or biopsy upon first recurrence.

candidate_evidence.quote: Patients receive temozolomide PO QD on days 1-5 of each cycle and selinexor PO QD on days 8 and 15 of each cycle.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Official: A Phase 1 and Randomized Phase 2 Trial of Selinexor and Temozolomide in Recurrent Glioblastoma

role_evidence.quote: Testing the Addition of an Anti-cancer Drug, Selinexor, to the Usual Chemotherapy Treatment (Temozolomide) for Brain Tumors That Have Returned After Previous Treatment

agents.drug_class_hint: selective inhibitor of nuclear export (XPO1/CRM1 inhibitor)
agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: It works by blocking a protein called CRM1, which may keep cancer cells from growing and may kill them.

role_evidence.quote: compares the effect of this combination therapy versus the usual chemotherapy alone (temozolomide) in treating patients with glioblastoma that has come back (recurrent)

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: It works by damaging the cell's deoxyribonucleic acid and may kill tumor cells and slow down or stop tumor growth.

coder_notes: Randomized phase 2: TMZ + placebo (registered ACTIVE_COMPARATOR) vs TMZ + selinexor; phase 1 used TMZ + selinexor (Group II). TMZ is given in both arms at recurrence and called the usual chemotherapy, coded soc_backbone. MGMT methylation and IDH-wildtype are entry requirements (never candidate-matched). The exploratory selinexor response signature is coded candidate_matched true because the record explicitly links it to selinexor response; P53, EGFR and Mcl-1 coded false as no mechanism linking them to XPO1 inhibition is stated (adjudicator may treat all as selinexor-linked). Blood sample collection planned but no PK or PD measurement stated.
